core_obligations: (4) implies (1) (proof lines 1536-1541): if every affine open is closed, then the intersection of two members of an affine open covering is a closed subset of an affine scheme, hence quasi-compact, which by the criterion means that X is quasi-separated.

(1) implies (2) (proof lines 1543-1551): if X is quasi-separated then each intersection U_i cap U_j is a quasi-compact open of U_i, hence closed, so the inclusion is an open immersion with closed image, hence a closed immersion; in particular the intersection is affine and the restriction map on rings is surjective, which by the criterion means that X is separated.

(2) implies (3) and (3) implies (4) (proof lines 1553-1565): separatedness gives disjoint open neighbourhoods of two points in a common affine open and, if the second point lies outside, an affine intersection which is closed in one piece; conversely, if X is Hausdorff then an affine open, being quasi-compact, is closed.

Final statements (proof lines 1567-1584): assuming the equivalent conditions, two distinct points are separated by an affine open containing one and not the other, which exhibits a decomposition of X into disjoint open and closed pieces, so connected components are points; and a quasi-compact open written as a union of n affine opens is affine by induction on n, the case n = 2 following from the decomposition of the union into the three pieces U_1 minus U_2, the intersection and U_2 minus U_1, each of which is affine.
proof_roadmap: Run the cycle of implications on an affine open covering, using the criteria for quasi-separatedness and separatedness.
Use Hausdorffness and quasi-compactness for the last implication.
Deduce that connected components are points and that quasi-compact opens are affine by induction.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the equivalence, for a scheme X of dimension zero, of quasi-separatedness, separatedness, Hausdorffness and the closedness of every affine open, and shows that then the connected components of X are points and every quasi-compact open is affine (statement lines 1519-1534). The proof (proof lines 1536-1587) runs the cycle of implications through the standard criteria on affine open coverings, and then deduces the two structural statements by a separation argument and an induction on the number of affine pieces. H2: a cycle of implications plus two structural deductions, written out in full.
